title: Top Food Processors for Faster Meal Prep (2026)
summary: The Cuisinart Custom 14 Cup is our top pick, named best by both Tom's Guide and America's Test Kitchen, with the Hamilton Beach 70730 for tight budgets and the Breville Sous Chef 16 for people who want every attachment.
method: Picks come from Tom's Guide (food processor guide updated May 15, 2026, which sliced, shredded, chopped, pureed and measured noise) and America's Test Kitchen (published Aug 4, 2026, which tested models on chopping, shredding, slicing, emulsifying and dough). Both name the Cuisinart Custom 14 Cup their top pick.
assumptions: Prices change often, so we quote what each source showed and tell you to check the current price. Where the two sources disagree, we say so, for example on the Magimix. We left out the KitchenAid 13 Cup, which Tom's Guide calls best for slicing but America's Test Kitchen recommends only with reservations.

products.name: Cuisinart Custom 14 Cup (DFP-14BCNY)
why: Both Tom's Guide and America's Test Kitchen name it their top pick. Tom's Guide measured just 65.2 dB, far quieter than the 79.2 dBA of the Magimix 14 Cup, and sliced a whole russet potato in two seconds and shredded cheddar in 10.
America's Test Kitchen calls it powerful, precise and compact for its large capacity, with a simple bowl and blade design that is easy to handle and clean. Its three blades store inside the bowl.
specs: 14-cup bowl, 720W motor, two control levers
Slicing disk, shredding disk and chopping blade stored in the bowl
Tom's Guide's price box showed $299.95, marked down to $194.73; America's Test Kitchen showed $230 at Amazon; check the current price
cons: America's Test Kitchen notes a redesigned blade left slightly bigger gaps, so it could not make a single-batch mayonnaise
products.best_for: Most home cooks who want one dependable, quiet full-size machine
products.skip_if: You only chop a little at a time and want something small

products.name: Cuisinart Pro Custom 11 (DLC-8SY)
why: America's Test Kitchen's Best Buy and a slightly smaller sibling of its winner. It shares the neat shape, precise processing and simple controls, and it aced chopping, slicing and shredding.
It adds an easy-to-clean flat lid for jobs like pie dough or salsa and an extra disk for thin slices, and its blade sits low enough to make a single batch of mayonnaise.
specs: 11-cup bowl, 625W motor, liquid maximum 2.25 cups
Two slicing disks, shredding disk and flat lid
America's Test Kitchen showed $200 at Amazon, down from $220; check the current price
pros: Handled a double batch of pizza dough
cons: Slightly less powerful and smaller than the 14-cup
The pusher is attached to a sleeve, so cleaning is a little fussier
products.best_for: Cooks who want near-winner performance for a bit less money
products.skip_if: You regularly make very large batches
products.amazon_listing: Cuisinart Food Processor, Dishwasher Safe 11-Cup Food Processor with Slicing & Shredding D

products.name: Hamilton Beach Bowl Scraper 10 Cup (70730)
why: Tom's Guide's best-value and budget pick. Its 450W motor chopped an onion in three seconds and grated cheddar in five, making it one of the fastest machines tested, and it handled sticky cookie dough with no strain.
The built-in manual bowl scraper clears the sides without opening the lid, which saves time. Tom's Guide says it is a bargain for under $60.
specs: 10-cup bowl, 450W, two speeds, 6.9 lb
Large feed chute, 1-year warranty
Tom's Guide's price box showed $69.95, marked down to $50.30; check the current price
cons: The scraper stops about an inch from the bottom
Light body rocks a little with dough
products.best_for: Budget shoppers who want a capable, no-frills processor
products.amazon_listing: Easy Clean Bowl Scraper for Hamilton Beach Food Processor 70733J, 70730 | fits 10-cup food

products.name: Breville Paradice 9
why: Tom's Guide's most versatile pick. All its attachments, including a dicing kit, adjustable slicer and dough blade, store inside the main bowl, which keeps a small kitchen tidy.
It blitzed rock-hard dried sourdough into breadcrumbs, turned a head of cauliflower into even rice, and its dicing attachment, rare at this size, made quick work of potatoes and fruit.
specs: 9-cup bowl, 625W, 4.5-inch feed chute, 5.5 lb
Dicing kit, adjustable slicer and dough blade stored in the bowl
Tom's Guide's price box showed $399.95; check the current price
cons: Food can get stuck in the dicing attachment
products.best_for: People who want one machine to replace a mandoline and other gadgets
products.skip_if: You only need basic chopping on a budget

products.name: Breville Sous Chef 16
why: America's Test Kitchen's upgrade pick for people who want every attachment. It comes with a 2.5-cup mini bowl, a french fry slicer and an adjustable slicer, and a dicing kit is available separately.
It shredded, sliced and chopped quickly and evenly with minimal waste, made smooth pizza dough with no motor struggle, and has simple controls, a count-up timer and a short, powerful pulse.
specs: 16-cup bowl with 2.5-cup mini bowl, liquid maximum 5 cups
Adjustable slicer, french fry disk, reversible shredder, S-blade, dough blade
America's Test Kitchen showed $500 at Amazon; check the current price
pros: Clear markings on the base and bowl
cons: Multi-part blades are a bit annoying to assemble
The lid has nooks that need detailed cleaning
products.best_for: Keen cooks with counter space who will use the extras
products.skip_if: You want a simple, small machine

products.name: Magimix Food Processor 14 Cup
why: Tom's Guide's most durable pick. It is built in France with a 30-year motor warranty and a 950W motor that sliced a potato in four seconds and handled cookie dough well, and a three-bowl system (6, 12 and 14 cups) lets you process a whole recipe without washing.

America's Test Kitchen tested the Magimix Compact 4200 XL and recommended it, but found it left streaks in a yogurt blending test and some oversize carrot and cheese pieces, so its all-round results were not top tier.
specs: 14-cup main bowl plus 12-cup and 6-cup bowls, 950W, 17 lb
30-year motor warranty
Tom's Guide's price box showed $399; check the current price
cons: Large, with a bulky storage case
Much louder than the Cuisinart in Tom's Guide's test (79.2 dBA)
America's Test Kitchen found uneven chopping and shredding
products.best_for: Serious cooks who want a long-lasting machine and have space for it
products.skip_if: You have a small kitchen or want top all-round results

products.name: KitchenAid Cordless Top Down Food Chopper
products.short: KitchenAid Cordless Top Down Food Chopper
why: Tom's Guide's most compact pick, a 3.5-cup cordless chopper that is light, portable and easy to tuck into a drawer. It made fresh salsa in under 10 seconds with three pulses and minced a carrot in seconds.
The battery works with other KitchenAid Go tools. It is not good at smooth purees, though: Tom's Guide's hummus stayed slightly chunky even after repeated scraping.
specs: 3.5-cup bowl, 240W, battery powered, 2.82 lb
One giant top power button
Tom's Guide cites roughly $99 with a battery and its price box showed $69.99; check the current price
pros: Battery fits the KitchenAid Go range
products.best_for: Small kitchens and cooks who only chop small amounts
products.skip_if: You want to slice, shred or knead dough

tips.title: How to choose
items: America's Test Kitchen thinks 11 cups or more is the most useful size for most home cooks, since it can chop, slice and knead small and large amounts.
Tom's Guide measured 65.2 dB on the Cuisinart 14 Cup and 93.9 dB on the Hamilton Beach, so budget models can be much louder.
America's Test Kitchen says most tasks need only chopping, slicing and shredding blades, and extra attachments add cost, storage and cleaning.
Look for a responsive pulse button.
America's Test Kitchen says a short, quick pulse gives you control over chop size and avoids over-processing.

faq: What is the best food processor overall?
Both Tom's Guide and America's Test Kitchen pick the Cuisinart Custom 14 Cup.
What is the best cheap food processor?
Tom's Guide picks the Hamilton Beach Bowl Scraper 10 Cup, which it says costs under $60, but it is very loud.
Is there a good small option?
Tom's Guide picks the KitchenAid Cordless Top Down Food Chopper, a 3.5-cup cordless chopper that is not suited to purees.
Is a food processor with more attachments worth it?
America's Test Kitchen recommends the Breville Sous Chef 16 only if you will use the extras and have the space and budget.
